package model

import (
	"encoding/json/v2"
	"testing"
	"time"
	"uuid"

	"codecfixture/other"
)

// Twins of every subject: the same fields, and no codec.
//
// A defined type does not inherit the methods declared on its source, so the
// standard library reflects over a twin while the subject itself dispatches to
// what forge wrote — and comparing the two is the whole of this file.
//
// A twin holding a struct has to hold a twin of it rather than the struct. A
// method is promoted from an embedded field and a field's own methods are used
// for that field, so a twin that kept Address where its source had one would
// have forge's codec called for that part of it, and the comparison would be
// between forge's output and forge's output.
//
// Exported, because reflection cannot write through an embedded pointer to an
// unexported type — which would make the one shape this file exists to check
// the one it could not read back.
type (
	ScalarsTwin    Scalars
	NamedTwin      Named
	TaggedTwin     Tagged
	CompositesTwin Composites
	AddressTwin    Address
	ReflectiveTwin Reflective

	// Stamped keeps its Stamp: the field carries a codec the author wrote, and
	// what forge does with one is call it — so both sides of the comparison
	// reach the same hand-written codec, which is the claim being made. Dated
	// keeps its Epoch for the same reason, with the codec in the one shape
	// generated code reaches through the standard library rather than calling.
	StampedTwin Stamped
	WeighedTwin Weighed
	DatedTwin   Dated

	// Omitting keeps its Address and Composites: what is under test here is
	// whether a member is written at all, and both sides reach the same codec
	// for the members that are.
	OmittingTwin Omitting
	NamingTwin   Naming

	// These keep their field types for the reason Stamped keeps its Stamp: what
	// is under test is what the field's own type carries, so both sides of the
	// comparison have to reach the same thing. Three of them carry a text codec
	// the standard library reaches for and forge must reach for too; three
	// carry something that only looks like one, and what is being checked there
	// is that neither side is fooled.
	ColouredTwin Coloured
	AppendedTwin Appended
	AliasingTwin Aliasing
	AgedTwin     Aged
	OddlyTwin    Oddly
	VariedTwin   Varied

	// Timed keeps its time.Time fields, which is the comparison the identity
	// asks for: the standard library reaches the type's own formatter through
	// its methods, forge writes it straight into the buffer, and the wire is
	// where the two claims meet. Identified keeps its uuid.UUID for the text
	// codec both sides reach; Preferred and Escaping keep their scalars so the
	// half taken and the escaping detour are each held against the library.
	TimedTwin      Timed
	IdentifiedTwin Identified
	PreferredTwin  Preferred
	EscapingTwin   Escaping
)

type NestedTwin struct {
	Home    AddressTwin
	Work    *AddressTwin
	Visited []AddressTwin
}

type EmbeddedTwin struct {
	AddressTwin
	Name string
}

// AskedTwin carries the option its source carries, so the comparison is
// between what forge does with ",embed" and what the standard library does
// with it rather than between the option and Go's anonymity.
type AskedTwin struct {
	AddressTwin `json:",embed"`
	Name        string
}

type RenamedTwin struct {
	AddressTwin `json:"address"`
	Name        string
}

type BehindTwin struct {
	*AddressTwin
	Name string
}

type ChainTwin struct {
	Name string    `json:"name,omitempty"`
	Next *ChainTwin `json:"next,omitempty"`
}

type CyclicTwin struct {
	Name string
	Next *CyclicTwin
}

func TestScalars(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Scalars{
		{},
		{
			Bool: true, String: "hello, world", Int: -3, Int8: -128, Int16: 32767,
			Int32: -2147483648, Int64: 9007199254740993, Uint: 7, Uint16: 65535,
			Uint32: 4294967295, Uint64: 18446744073709551615, Float32: 1.1, Float64: 1.1,
		},
		{String: "quotes \" and \\ backslashes, ünïcode, and a\ttab"},
	} {
		agree(t, held, ScalarsTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestNamed(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Named{{}, {Temp: -40.5, Label: "warm", Count: 12}} {
		agree(t, held, NamedTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestTagged(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Tagged{
		{},
		{Renamed: "a", Hidden: "never written", Zero: 1, Empty: []int{1, 2}, Plain: "p"},
		{Empty: []int{}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, TaggedTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestComposites(t *testing.T) {
	text := "pointed at"

	for _, held := range []Composites{
		{},
		{
			Strings: []string{"a", "b"}, Numbers: []int{1, -2},
			Nested: [][]string{{"x"}, {}, nil}, Fixed: [3]int{7, 8, 9},
			Lookup: map[string]int{"z": 1, "a": 2, "m": 3},
			Deep:   map[string][]string{"k": {"v1", "v2"}, "j": nil},
			Pointer: &text, Bytes: []byte{0, 1, 254, 255},
		},
		{Strings: []string{}, Lookup: map[string]int{}, Bytes: []byte{}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, CompositesTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestAddress(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Address{{}, {City: "Oslo", Post: "0150"}} {
		agree(t, held, AddressTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestNested(t *testing.T) {
	work := Address{City: "Kyoto", Post: "600"}

	for _, held := range []Nested{
		{},
		{
			Home: Address{City: "Oslo", Post: "0150"}, Work: &work,
			Visited: []Address{{City: "Lima"}, {Post: "X"}},
		},
	} {
		agree(t, held, nestedLike(held))
	}
}

func TestEmbedded(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Embedded{{}, {Address: Address{City: "Cairo", Post: "11511"}, Name: "n"}} {
		agree(t, held, EmbeddedTwin{AddressTwin: AddressTwin(held.Address), Name: held.Name})
	}
}

// TestAsked holds the written option to the same output the implied one gets.
// Promotion is what embed means, so the members come out where the embedded
// field is and not inside an object of their own.
func TestAsked(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Asked{{}, {Address: Address{City: "Lima", Post: "15074"}, Name: "n"}} {
		agree(t, held, AskedTwin{AddressTwin: AddressTwin(held.Address), Name: held.Name})
	}
}

func TestRenamed(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Renamed{{}, {Address: Address{City: "Lisbon"}, Name: "n"}} {
		agree(t, held, RenamedTwin{AddressTwin: AddressTwin(held.Address), Name: held.Name})
	}
}

func TestBehind(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Behind{{}, {Address: &Address{City: "Accra"}, Name: "n"}} {
		twin := BehindTwin{Name: held.Name}
		if held.Address != nil {
			one := AddressTwin(*held.Address)
			twin.AddressTwin = &one
		}
		agree(t, held, twin)
	}
}

func TestReflective(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Reflective{
		{},
		{Name: "n", Extra: map[string]any{"k": 1.5, "a": "text"}},
		{Extra: []any{1.0, "two", true, nil}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, ReflectiveTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestStamped(t *testing.T) {
	also := Stamp{Seconds: 17}

	for _, held := range []Stamped{{}, {At: Stamp{Seconds: -1}, Also: &also, Name: "n"}} {
		agree(t, held, StampedTwin(held))
	}
}

// A codec that speaks the streaming interface is reached through the standard
// library from forge's side and from reflection's, so both arrive at the same
// hand-written methods by different roads.
func TestDated(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Dated{{}, {At: Epoch{S: -3}, Name: "n"}} {
		agree(t, held, DatedTwin(held))
	}

	var forged Dated
	var reflected DatedTwin
	readAlike(t, `{"At":9,"Name":"x"}`, &forged, &reflected)
	readAlike(t, `{"At":"nine"}`, &forged, &reflected)
}

// A borrowed read fills the same value the copying read fills; what differs is
// only whose bytes the strings are, and this document outlives the value.
func TestBorrowedReadsWhatCopyingReads(t *testing.T) {
	doc := []byte(`{"At":5,"Also":7,"Name":"n"}`)

	var copied, borrowed Stamped
	if err := copied.UnmarshalJSON(doc); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := borrowed.UnmarshalJSONBorrowed(doc); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	first, err := json.Marshal(copied, json.Deterministic(true))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	second, err := json.Marshal(borrowed, json.Deterministic(true))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if string(first) != string(second) {
		t.Errorf("the copying read holds %s and the borrowing one %s", first, second)
	}
}

// A named scalar with a text codec goes out as the text, from both sides.
//
// The standard library asks a type for a text codec before it writes the form
// underneath, and so does forge. A colour written as the number behind it would
// say nothing to a reader and would move the day somebody inserted a colour
// above green.
func TestColoured(t *testing.T) {
	green := Green
	for _, held := range []Coloured{
		{},
		{Shade: Green, Name: "n"},
		{Shade: Red, Accent: &green, Name: "n"},
	} {
		agree(t, held, ColouredTwin(held))
	}
}

// A type whose only writing half is the appender is written through it.
//
// encoding.TextAppender is the newer of the two halves and a type may carry it
// alone, so a reader that asked only for MarshalText would write the number for
// a type that had said how it reads.
func TestAppended(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Appended{{}, {Held: 1}} {
		agree(t, held, AppendedTwin(held))
	}
}

// A type carrying the codec that came before this one is written as the older
// codec writes it, by both sides.
//
// The standard library asks for that pair before it asks for a text codec.
// Forge reads neither pair, so it writes the form underneath — which is what
// the older codec here writes too. A forge that had taken the text codec
// instead would be the one reader in the ecosystem writing a string.
func TestAged(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Aged{{}, {Held: 3}} {
		agree(t, held, AgedTwin(held))
	}
}

// A method named as a text codec's half and shaped like nothing is not one.
//
// The standard library reads the shape as well as the name and ignores this
// pair, writing the number underneath. So does forge, which is what keeps a
// generated call from being written with the wrong number of results — and what
// keeps the two agreeing about a type whose author very nearly wrote a codec.
func TestOddly(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Oddly{{}, {Held: 4}} {
		agree(t, held, OddlyTwin(held))
	}
}

// A text codec spelled through aliases is a text codec.
//
// An alias is the same type, so a codec written against one satisfies the same
// interface — and a reader of the signature that compared spellings rather than
// types would write the number for a value the standard library writes as its
// name.
func TestAliasing(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Aliasing{{}, {Held: 1}} {
		agree(t, held, AliasingTwin(held))
	}
}

// A text codec whose reader takes its bytes one at a time is not one.
//
// A variadic parameter is a slice to the function and one value to every
// caller. Neither the standard library nor forge accepts it, so both write the
// number — and the pair agreeing is what says forge read the shape rather than
// only the name.
func TestVaried(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Varied{{}, {Held: 5}} {
		agree(t, held, VariedTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestWeighed(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Weighed{{}, {Mass: Weight{Grams: 900}, Name: "n"}} {
		agree(t, held, WeighedTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestOmitting(t *testing.T) {
	text := "there"

	for _, held := range []Omitting{
		{},
		{
			Text: "t", Count: 1, Flag: true, List: []int{1}, Lookup: map[string]int{"k": 1},
			Ptr: &text, Blob: []byte{1},
			ZeroText: "z", ZeroFlag: true, ZeroFloat: 0.5,
			ZeroStruct: Address{City: "Bern"}, ZeroArray: [2]int{1, 2}, ZeroList: []int{3},
			ZeroPtr: &Address{Post: "P"}, ZeroHolder: Composites{Strings: []string{"s"}},
			ZeroFix: [4]byte{1, 0, 0, 2},
			ZeroSlices: [2][]int{{1}, nil},
			ZeroBehind: Behind{Address: &Address{City: "Suva"}, Name: "b"},
			EmptyBehind: Behind{Name: "e"},
			BothList: []int{1}, BothText: "b",
		},
		// Every one of them empty in the JSON sense but not obviously so in Go:
		// an allocated slice and map are not nil, and a pointer to a zero value
		// is not a nil pointer.
		{List: []int{}, Lookup: map[string]int{}, Blob: []byte{}, ZeroList: []int{}, ZeroPtr: &Address{}},
		// An allocated empty slice under both options. omitzero says it is not
		// the zero value and omitempty says it is empty on the wire, so the
		// disjunction leaves it out and taking only the first would write it.
		{BothList: []int{}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, OmittingTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestNaming(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Naming{{}, {UserID: 1, JSONValue: "v", HTTPServer: "s", ID: 2, Name: "n"}} {
		agree(t, held, NamingTwin(held))
	}
}

func TestCyclic(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Cyclic{{}, {Name: "head", Next: &Cyclic{Name: "tail"}}} {
		agree(t, held, cyclicLike(held))
	}
}

// nestedLike and cyclicLike build the twin of a value whose fields are structs,
// which no conversion can do: the two types differ in exactly the field types
// that had to differ.
func nestedLike(held Nested) NestedTwin {
	out := NestedTwin{Home: AddressTwin(held.Home)}

	if held.Work != nil {
		one := AddressTwin(*held.Work)
		out.Work = &one
	}
	for _, one := range held.Visited {
		out.Visited = append(out.Visited, AddressTwin(one))
	}
	return out
}

func cyclicLike(held Cyclic) CyclicTwin {
	out := CyclicTwin{Name: held.Name}
	if held.Next != nil {
		one := cyclicLike(*held.Next)
		out.Next = &one
	}
	return out
}

// agree checks that forge's codec and the standard library's reflection produce
// the same bytes for one value, and read the same value back out of them.
//
// Both directions, because they fail differently. A writer that disagrees sends
// the wrong thing; a reader that disagrees accepts what the writer sent and
// stores something else, which is the failure that survives a round trip through
// one program and appears in another.
//
// Deterministic, because the one place forge's writer differs on purpose is map
// member order: forge sorts, so that generated output does not change between
// runs. Asking the standard library for the same thing compares the two on the
// question actually at issue rather than on Go's map iteration.
func agree[T, U any](t *testing.T, forged T, reflected U) {
	t.Helper()

	written, err := json.Marshal(forged, json.Deterministic(true))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("forge's codec would not write %#v: %v", forged, err)
	}

	want, err := json.Marshal(reflected, json.Deterministic(true))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the standard library would not write %#v: %v", reflected, err)
	}

	if string(written) != string(want) {
		t.Errorf("forge wrote\n\t%s\nand the standard library wrote\n\t%s\nfor %#v",
			written, want, forged)
		return
	}

	// Read back by both, then written again by both. Comparing the two values
	// directly is not available — they are different types, which is the whole
	// arrangement — and rewriting is the stronger check anyway: it says the two
	// readers produced values that mean the same thing rather than that they
	// filled the same fields.
	var back T
	if err := json.Unmarshal(written, &back); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("forge's codec would not read back %s: %v", written, err)
	}

	var reference U
	if err := json.Unmarshal(want, &reference); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the standard library would not read back %s: %v", want, err)
	}

	first, err := json.Marshal(back, json.Deterministic(true))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("forge's codec would not rewrite what it read: %v", err)
	}
	second, err := json.Marshal(reference, json.Deterministic(true))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the standard library would not rewrite what it read: %v", err)
	}

	if string(first) != string(second) {
		t.Errorf("after reading %s back, forge holds\n\t%s\nand the standard library holds\n\t%s",
			written, first, second)
	}
}

// Twins for the shapes whose own fields are structs, which no conversion
// reaches: the two types differ in exactly the field types that had to differ.
type (
	PointedTwin  Pointed
	MeasuredTwin Measured
	DeepTwin     Deep
	PlaceTwin    other.Place
	HollowTwin   Hollow
	ScalaredTwin Scalared
	BorrowedTwin Borrowed
	MarkedTwin   Marked
	NilableTwin  Nilable
	BufferedTwin Buffered
)

type SettledTwin struct {
	LeftTwin
	RightTwin
	Shared string
}

type (
	LeftTwin  Left
	RightTwin Right
)

type ShadowTwin struct {
	DeepTwin
	Shared string
	Only   string
}

type HollowedTwin struct {
	Ptr  *HollowTwin `json:"ptr,omitempty"`
	Text *string     `json:"text,omitempty"`
	Name string      `json:"name,omitempty"`
}

type ElsewhereTwin struct {
	Temp   other.Celsius
	Name   other.Label
	Many   []other.Celsius
	Lookup map[string]other.Label
	Ptr    *other.Celsius
	Where  PlaceTwin
	Places []PlaceTwin
}

// A pointer to a number is read into a temporary rather than into a field, and
// a decoder that let its own temporaries shadow that one reads the value and
// then throws it away.
func TestPointed(t *testing.T) {
	var (
		big   = int64(9007199254740993)
		num   = -3
		small = int8(-128)
		count = uint32(4294967295)
		ratio = float32(0.5)
		warm  = Celsius(-40.5)
		text  = "pointed"
		flag  = true
	)

	for _, held := range []Pointed{
		{},
		{Big: &big, Num: &num, Small: &small, Count: &count, Ratio: &ratio, Warm: &warm, Text: &text, Flag: &flag},
	} {
		agree(t, held, PointedTwin(held))
	}
}

// A codec names every type it reaches into, and a file that binds none of them
// does not compile. Reaching one across a package boundary is what makes that
// visible: the enclosing type's own spelling says nothing about the package its
// members come from.
func TestElsewhere(t *testing.T) {
	warm := other.Celsius(21.5)

	for _, held := range []Elsewhere{
		{},
		{
			Temp: -40.5, Name: "label", Many: []other.Celsius{1, 2},
			Lookup: map[string]other.Label{"k": "v"}, Ptr: &warm,
			Where: other.Place{City: "Doha"}, Places: []other.Place{{City: "Lima"}},
		},
	} {
		agree(t, held, elsewhereLike(held))
	}
}

// A type that says for itself when it is empty is asked rather than compared.
func TestMeasured(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Measured{{}, {M: Measure{Amount: 3}, Name: "n"}, {M: Measure{Amount: -1}, Name: "unset"}} {
		agree(t, held, MeasuredTwin(held))
	}
}

// A member that wins a shadowed name keeps its own place in the object rather
// than taking the place of the one it beat.
func TestShadow(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Shadow{
		{},
		{Shared: "own", Only: "o", Deep: Deep{Shared: "deep", Extra: "e"}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, ShadowTwin{DeepTwin: DeepTwin(held.Deep), Shared: held.Shared, Only: held.Only})
	}
}

// A pointer to something that renders empty is empty, however present the
// pointer is.
func TestHollowed(t *testing.T) {
	var (
		empty = ""
		text  = "there"
	)

	for _, held := range []Hollowed{
		{},
		{Ptr: &Hollow{}, Text: &empty},
		{Ptr: &Hollow{Text: "t"}, Text: &text, Name: "n"},
	} {
		twin := HollowedTwin{Text: held.Text, Name: held.Name}
		if held.Ptr != nil {
			one := HollowTwin(*held.Ptr)
			twin.Ptr = &one
		}
		agree(t, held, twin)
	}
}

// elsewhereLike builds the twin of a value holding structs from another package.
func elsewhereLike(held Elsewhere) ElsewhereTwin {
	out := ElsewhereTwin{
		Temp: held.Temp, Name: held.Name, Many: held.Many,
		Lookup: held.Lookup, Ptr: held.Ptr, Where: PlaceTwin(held.Where),
	}
	for _, one := range held.Places {
		out.Places = append(out.Places, PlaceTwin(one))
	}
	return out
}

// What a reader does with a document it did not write is where a codec is
// actually used, and it is the half a round trip cannot reach.
//
// Feeding a codec its own output only ever asks whether it agrees with itself.
// Every document here is one somebody else could send: a null where a number
// was expected, a string where a number was, an array of the wrong length, a
// member nobody declared. What matters is that forge and the standard library
// reach the same answer — the same value, or an error where the other errs.
func TestReadingWhatSomebodyElseWrote(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []string{
		// Nulls, which are a value rather than a disagreement.
		`{"Bool":null,"String":null,"Int":null,"Float64":null}`,
		`{"Home":null,"Work":null,"Visited":null}`,
		`{"Strings":null,"Lookup":null,"Fixed":null,"Pointer":null,"Bytes":null}`,

		// Numbers the target cannot hold, which jsontext reads into a width of
		// its own before anything narrower is asked about.
		`{"Int8":300}`,
		`{"Int16":70000}`,
		`{"Int32":3000000000}`,
		`{"Uint16":70000}`,
		`{"Uint32":5000000000}`,
		`{"Float32":1e40}`,
		`{"Float32":1.0000001}`,
		`{"Float32":1.1}`,
		`{"Float64":1.1}`,
		`{"Int8":-300}`,
		`{"Uint":-1}`,

		// Kinds the target cannot hold.
		`{"Int":"5"}`,
		`{"String":5}`,
		`{"Bool":1}`,
		`{"Int":1.5}`,
		`{"Int8":99999999999999999999}`,
		`{"Uint":-1}`,

		// Lengths an array cannot hold.
		`{"Fixed":[1]}`,
		`{"Fixed":[1,2,3,4]}`,
		`{"Fixed":[1,2,3]}`,

		// Shapes where an object or an array was expected.
		`{"Home":[1,2]}`,
		`{"Strings":{"a":1}}`,
		`{"Lookup":[1]}`,

		// Members nobody declared, holding whatever they like.
		`{"nope":{"deep":[1,{"deeper":null}]},"String":"kept"}`,

		// Nothing at all, and a null for the whole of it.
		`{}`,
		`null`,
	}

	for _, doc := range cases {
		t.Run(doc, func(t *testing.T) {
			// Read into a target that already holds something, because that is
			// what a reader in a loop does and it is where leaving a value
			// untouched and zeroing it come apart.
			forged := Scalars{Bool: true, String: "before", Int: 9, Int8: 1, Uint: 2, Float64: 1.5}
			reflected := ScalarsTwin(forged)
			readAlike(t, doc, &forged, &reflected)

			held := Composites{Strings: []string{"before"}, Fixed: [3]int{7, 8, 9}}
			heldTwin := CompositesTwin(held)
			readAlike(t, doc, &held, &heldTwin)

			nested := Nested{Home: Address{City: "before"}}
			nestedTwin := nestedLike(nested)
			readAlike(t, doc, &nested, &nestedTwin)
		})
	}
}

// readAlike reads one document with both codecs and compares what each made of
// it, error included.
func readAlike[T, U any](t *testing.T, doc string, forged *T, reflected *U) {
	t.Helper()

	forgedErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(doc), forged)
	reflectedErr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(doc), reflected)

	if (forgedErr != nil) != (reflectedErr != nil) {
		t.Errorf("reading %s into %T: forge said %v and the standard library said %v",
			doc, *forged, forgedErr, reflectedErr)
		return
	}
	if forgedErr != nil {
		// Both refused. What they say need not match word for word — the
		// messages are the standard library's to word — only that both refused.
		return
	}

	first, err := json.Marshal(forged, json.Deterministic(true))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rewriting what forge read: %v", err)
	}
	second, err := json.Marshal(reflected, json.Deterministic(true))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("rewriting what the standard library read: %v", err)
	}

	if string(first) != string(second) {
		t.Errorf("after reading %s, forge holds\n\t%s\nand the standard library holds\n\t%s",
			doc, first, second)
	}
}

// A member nothing can predict is written and then looked at, which is the only
// way to answer emptiness for something somebody else writes.
//
// The map is here for the options rather than for the shape: a member encoded
// without the ones the caller gave would order its keys however the map felt
// like, which is the one thing this codec's output is not allowed to do.
func TestBuffered(t *testing.T) {
	at := Stamp{Seconds: 3}
	zero := Stamp{}

	for _, held := range []Buffered{
		{},
		{One: at, Ptr: &at, Extra: map[string]any{"z": 1.0, "a": 2.0, "m": 3.0, "q": 4.0}, Name: "n"},
		// Each at a value that renders empty or nearly so: a zero stamp writes
		// 0, which is not empty, and an allocated-but-empty map is.
		{One: zero, Ptr: &zero, Extra: map[string]any{}},
		{Extra: []any{}},
		{Extra: ""},
		{Extra: nil, Name: "only"},
	} {
		agree(t, held, BufferedTwin(held))
	}
}

// A type that reaches itself is written and looked at too, and the recursion
// ends where the chain does.
func TestChain(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Chain{
		{},
		{Name: "head"},
		{Next: &Chain{}},
		{Name: "head", Next: &Chain{Name: "tail"}},
		{Name: "head", Next: &Chain{Next: &Chain{}}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, chainLike(held))
	}
}

func chainLike(held Chain) ChainTwin {
	out := ChainTwin{Name: held.Name}
	if held.Next != nil {
		one := chainLike(*held.Next)
		out.Next = &one
	}
	return out
}

// A member asked to be omitted at its zero value, where that value is not
// something a composite literal can spell.
func TestMarked(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Marked{
		{},
		{At: 5, Extra: map[string]any{"k": 1.0}},
		{At: 0, Extra: nil},
		{At: -1, Extra: []any{}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, MarkedTwin(held))
	}
}

// A name two embedded structs both claim is settled by a field of the enclosing
// struct, which is a struct the standard library encodes without complaint.
func TestSettled(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Settled{
		{},
		{Shared: "own", Left: Left{Shared: "l"}, Right: Right{Shared: "r"}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, SettledTwin{
			LeftTwin: LeftTwin(held.Left), RightTwin: RightTwin(held.Right), Shared: held.Shared,
		})
	}
}

// A type reaching another package through named scalars alone.
func TestScalared(t *testing.T) {
	label := other.Label("l")

	for _, held := range []Scalared{{}, {Temp: 1.5, Many: []other.Celsius{2, -3}, Ptr: &label}} {
		agree(t, held, ScalaredTwin(held))
	}
}

// A type reaching another package only through members that name no package
// when they are written.
func TestBorrowed(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Borrowed{{}, {At: 17, B: Blob{1, 2, 254}}, {B: Blob{}}} {
		agree(t, held, BorrowedTwin(held))
	}
}

// A pointer to a type that writes itself, omitted when it is nil.
func TestNilable(t *testing.T) {
	at := Stamp{Seconds: 3}
	zero := Stamp{}

	for _, held := range []Nilable{{}, {At: &at, Name: "n"}, {At: &zero}, {Name: "only"}} {
		agree(t, held, NilableTwin(held))
	}
}

// A time goes onto the wire by identity, and the wire cannot tell.
//
// Forge appends the value straight into the buffer where the standard library
// calls the type's own MarshalJSON; the two are one formatter, and this is the
// comparison that keeps them so. The zone with an offset is here because the
// offset is part of what RFC 3339 writes, and the nanoseconds because trailing
// zeros are dropped and both sides have to drop them alike.
func TestTimed(t *testing.T) {
	at := time.Date(2026, 9, 4, 12, 30, 45, 123456789, time.UTC)
	shifted := time.Date(2001, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 700000000, time.FixedZone("", 3*3600+30*60))
	for _, held := range []Timed{
		{},
		{At: at, Started: at},
		{At: shifted, Maybe: &at, Seen: []time.Time{at, shifted, {}}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, TimedTwin(held))
	}
}

// A year RFC 3339 cannot carry is refused on the way out, from both sides.
//
// The formatter's verdict is part of what the identity borrowed, so the value
// the standard library refuses to write is refused here too rather than
// arriving somewhere as a document nothing can read back.
func TestTimedRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	held := Timed{At: time.Date(10000, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)}
	if _, err := json.Marshal(held); err == nil {
		t.Error("forge wrote a year RFC 3339 cannot carry")
	}
	if _, err := json.Marshal(TimedTwin(held)); err == nil {
		t.Error("the standard library wrote a year RFC 3339 cannot carry")
	}
}

// An identifier goes out as its hyphenated text, from both sides.
func TestIdentified(t *testing.T) {
	one := uuid.MustParse("0192aefb-74a0-7000-8000-1234567890ab")
	two := uuid.MustParse("ffffffff-ffff-ffff-ffff-ffffffffffff")
	for _, held := range []Identified{
		{},
		{ID: one, Maybe: &two, Batch: []uuid.UUID{one, two, {}}},
	} {
		agree(t, held, IdentifiedTwin(held))
	}
}

// Where a type carries both writing halves, the appender's answer is the one
// on the wire.
//
// The two halves here disagree on purpose and the reader accepts only the
// appender's answer, so this test fails twice over for a codec that took the
// other half: the bytes differ from the standard library's, and what was
// written cannot come back.
func TestPreferred(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Preferred{{}, {Held: 1}} {
		agree(t, held, PreferredTwin(held))
	}
}

// Text the appender writes straight into the document is escaped as though it
// had gone through the escaper from the start, because on this path it does —
// after the fact, and only when the scan says it must.
func TestEscaping(t *testing.T) {
	for _, held := range []Escaping{{}, {Held: 1}} {
		agree(t, held, EscapingTwin(held))
	}
}
